To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the growth rate of the economy can be improved by using the appropriate combination of taxes and quantitative controls, and that (2) the optimal policy design is dependent upon the relative importance of environmental quality in the utility function of the consumer

(i) optimal policies that combine quantity controls and optimal taxes (subsidies) are superior to optimal taxes (subbidies) alone; and (ii) the welfare gains from using optimal policies are greater the higher is the elasticity of substitution between the environment and capital.

(1) the optimal policy design depends on whether the regulator is able to observe and control individual agents’ actions, or only their outcomes (2) the optimal policy is more effective if the regulator can control the actions of the agents, and (3) a combination of optimal taxes and quantity controls can be more effective than an optimal tax or an optimal subsidy alone, if the regulator is able control the actions of agents
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimal use of economic policy instruments to achieve a given environmental objective, in this case, the preservation of a natural resource.
a dynamic economy in which environmental quality and economic activity are linked.
the design of optimal policy instruments that will lead to a higher level economic growth and a better environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal policy design is not a simple one and it depends on the nature of the environment and the production technology.

the optimal tax (subside) scheme is the best policy to use in the presence of an externality, but a combination of optimal tax (subidy) and optimal quantitative restrictions is the best policy in the presence of both an externality and a natural resource.
the optimal growth path is not necessarily the one that maximizes the welfare level of the representative individual.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the environment is a key factor to consider in optimal policy designs.
the optimal policy design depends on the relative importance of the environment in the utility and the production functions.
a policy mix of production taxes and subsidies and quantitative restrictions leads to a better economic growth than any single instrument.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulator can achieve a higher level of economic growth by designing optimal tax and subsidy schemes and quantity controls.
the environment should be considered in designing policies for long run growth and welfare.
environmental policy design should be considered jointly with other policy instruments to maximize social welfare and to achieve a desired rate of long run growth.
